name: Add-on
propertyCopy: Size, corner radius, label, placeholder, prefix and suffix are properties of the same component, not separate fields - change them below to check this field's style and states in the Live Preview.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Add-on is a single-line text field with a fixed, non-editable prefix and/or suffix segment attached directly to it - used when the value alone would be ambiguous or would force the user to retype a constant part of it every time. When to Use A value with a fixed protocol or domain prefix - https:// before a URL. A currency symbol on a price - $ before a numeric amount. A username handle with a fixed platform prefix - @ before a handle, or a fixed email domain suffix. When Not to Use A value with no natural constant part - use a plain Input - adding an empty or irrelevant add-on segment is just visual noise. A prefix/suffix that the user should be able to edit or choose - use a Select alongside the field, or a Group Button, instead of a fixed, non-editable add-on. Multiple independent constant parts on both sides that combine in complex ways - consider breaking the field into clearly labeled separate inputs instead. Best Practices Keep the add-on segment visually distinct but clearly non-editable (different background, no cursor) so users don't try to click into it. Use the add-on only for a genuinely constant part of the value - never for something that varies per use case. Make sure the combined value (prefix + typed value + suffix) is what actually gets submitted, not just displayed. Do and Don't Do Price£per month The add-ons carry the unit, so the input holds only the number the user actually has to type. Don't PriceSet the amount An add-on used as a label steals the width the value needs and leaves the field itself unlabelled. Add-ons are for units and fixed fragments, not instructions. Accessibility The prefix/suffix text is exposed to assistive technology alongside the field's label, so its meaning isn't lost for screen-reader users. The editable portion remains a real, independently focusable input - the add-on segments are not part of the tab order since they aren't interactive. Sufficient contrast between the add-on segment and the editable field, so the boundary between fixed and editable text is visually clear.
